validity.researcher_notes:
EXISTENCE: confirmed independently of GEM/wiki. The pipeline is a real, FERC-jurisdictional interstate offshore gas transmission line, not a GEM-only entity. Three independent origins: (1) Enbridge's own 'Energy Infrastructure Assets' factsheet PDF (owner/operator, p.79-80) names 'Mississippi Canyon Pipeline' explicitly and states it is a 30-inch, FERC-regulated offshore natural gas transmission pipeline, 44.5 miles (71.6 km) in the Mississippi Canyon Corridor of the Gulf of Mexico, delivering to a processing plant in Venice, LA, capacity 800 MMcf/d, status Operational. (2) Rextag Corporation (independent third-party pipeline-data vendor, not affiliated with Enbridge) states: 'Mississippi Canyon Gas Pipeline, LLC operates a small 44.5-mile pipeline offshore from the West Delta 143 Platform in the Gulf of Mexico to Venice, Louisiana... Owned by Enbridge, Inc., and operated by Mississippi Canyon Gas Pipeline, LLC'; its data table separately lists 'Miles of Pipeline: 45' and 'System Capacity: 0.8 Bcf/d'. (3) A genuinely independent government record: Federal Register notice (govinfo.gov, FR-1998-09-10, Docket No. TM99-1-134-000) shows 'Mississippi Canyon Gas Pipeline, LLC' tendering a FERC Gas Tariff filing on August 28, 1998 -- proof the entity was an active FERC-regulated natural-gas tariff filer by 1998, wholly independent of Enbridge's own materials. Two further Federal Register entries (federalregister.gov, 2000-08-22 and 2007-03-13) show the same LLC continuing to file FERC gas tariffs, corroborating multi-decade continuous operation consistent with the sheet's Status=operating.
CLASSIFICATION: correct. Enbridge's own factsheet explicitly labels it an 'offshore natural gas transmission pipeline' (not gathering/lateral), consistent with GEM's PipelineType and Fuel=Gas.
DUPLICATE: checked against all 50 rows in the batch-2 roster (Gulf Coast operating gas). No overlap in route, length, or diameter with any other row -- nearest offshore neighbors are P0204 Independence Trail (West Delta Block 68->GoM, 138 mi, 24in, 1000 MMcf/d), P0223 Nautilus (Ship Shoal 207/Green Canyon->Louisiana, 154 mi, 30in, 600 MMcf/d), and P0192 Garden Banks (GoM->GoM, 84 mi, 30in, 1000 MMcf/d) -- all distinct lengths/capacities/corridors from P0217's 44.5 mi/800 MMcf/d Mississippi-Canyon-to-Venice route. Not a relabel of any of these. Separately, a 1992 OTC conference paper ('Design and Installation of the 20-in. OD Mississippi Canyon Block 397 Gas Pipeline') describes a DIFFERENT, smaller-diameter (20-in) line at a specific block within the broader Mississippi Canyon area -- this is not GEM's P0217 (30-in, 44.5 mi, system-level trunk to Venice) and is not in the GEM roster, so it is not a duplicate concern for this database, just a note that 'Mississippi Canyon' as a place name covers multiple distinct pipeline projects in industry literature.
ATTRIBUTION: Owner1=Enbridge (100%) confirmed by two independent sources (Enbridge's own factsheet listing it among Enbridge assets, and Rextag's independent statement 'Owned by Enbridge, Inc.'). StartState/EndState = Louisiana on both ends is consistent with sources: the pipeline is entirely in the Gulf of Mexico OCS off Louisiana and lands at Venice, LA -- no attribution concern.
SPEC: Length (44.5 mi), Diameter (30 in), and Capacity (800 MMcf/d) all match exactly between GEM and BOTH the Enbridge factsheet and Rextag (Rextag's rounded '45 miles' / '0.8 Bcf/d' are consistent roundings of the same figures, not disagreements). No material spec disagreement found.
Opened/read to exhaustion: the full Enbridge 156-page factsheet PDF (searched for every GEM column: length, diameter, capacity, status, fuel, ownership -- no construction/proposal/in-service date or pressure value found anywhere in the document), the Rextag page (full text), the infopost.enbridge.com LINK posting page (confirms legal entity name 'Mississippi Canyon Gas Pipeline, LLC' and EIN-style ID 946822749, but is an Enbridge-hosted system so not independent from source 1), and the 1998 Federal Register PDF (full text). Of the 5 citations in this row's harvested wiki pool, 4 were opened live (Enbridge factsheet, infopost.enbridge.com, and both Wikipedia links); the 5th (bit.ly/2kAJ4T2) resolves to https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mississippi_Canyon_Pipeline, which returns 404 -- that Wikipedia article does not exist (dead link, not a GEM/existence concern since the pipeline's existence is independently confirmed above). The en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mississippi_Canyon citation is about the geographic seafloor canyon feature, not the pipeline, so it is relevant only as background for the StartLocation place name, not as a spec/existence source. infopost.spectraenergy.com (the pre-2017-merger legacy Spectra Energy URL) no longer resolves (NXDOMAIN) -- expected, since Spectra Energy merged into Enbridge in 2017 and its infopost system was consolidated into infopost.enbridge.com.
